questions.stem: Why are bond energy values described as averages?

options.text: Because instruments cannot measure them precisely
Because the exact bond energy varies depending on the molecular environment
Because bond energies change with temperature
Because only half the bonds break during a reaction

questions.explanation: Bond energies are averages because the exact energy of a particular bond varies depending on the molecule it is in. For example, a C-H bond in methane has a slightly different energy from a C-H bond in ethane. The average is taken across many different compounds.

questions.stem: The N≡N bond energy is 945 kJ/mol, which is very high. What does this tell us about nitrogen gas?

options.text: Nitrogen is very reactive because it has a lot of stored energy
Nitrogen is very unreactive because the triple bond is very strong and hard to break
Nitrogen has a low melting point because of its strong bond
Nitrogen easily forms compounds at room temperature

questions.explanation: The very high bond energy of the N≡N triple bond (945 kJ/mol) means a large amount of energy is needed to break it. This is why nitrogen gas is so unreactive and stable under normal conditions. The strong triple bond makes it difficult for nitrogen to react.
